title: King Aldric
content:
Biography Aldric is the 42nd monarch of Northwaldia. Known as the “Sage of the Terminal,” he is famous for his unconventional method of ruling his domain entirely via plain-text files and shell scripts.
He shares his throne with Queen Elysia, who oversees the kingdom’s cryptographic defenses. Unlike her husband, Elysia prefers a more “Debian-stable” approach to governance, leading to lively midnight debates in the royal court.
Early Life Aldric’s birth in the royal house of Northstar is often treated as the beginning of the modern Northwald succession.
Conflict with the South Currently, Aldric’s forces are engaged in a long-standing border dispute with South Isles. This war began not over land or gold, but over a disagreement regarding the default init system for the regional network.
Equipment and Tools Aldric is rarely seen without his enchanted mechanical keyboard, forged in the fires of Mount Git. It is said that when he types, the very fabric of the kingdom’s configuration files updates in real-time.

title: Queen Elysia
content:
Biography Queen Elysia is the co-ruler of Northwaldia. Known throughout the realms as “The Keeper of the Keys,” she manages the kingdom’s vast cryptographic archives and ensure the stability of the realm’s core services.
While her husband, King Aldric, focuses on rapid development and experimental “rolling” policies, Elysia is the voice of caution. She famously refused to update the kingdom’s primary firewall for three years, arguing that “if it isn’t broken, it’s secure.”
The Great Debate Elysia is widely respected for her patience during the midnight debates in the Citadel of Ice. While Aldric argues for the latest features of the newest kernels, Elysia maintains a fortress-like focus on uptime and reliability.
Diplomatic Stance In the conflict with Kingdom of Westwall, Elysia takes a defensive posture. She believes that a properly configured vault is more valuable than ten thousand swords.
Equipment Elysia carries a heavy ring of iron keys, each corresponding to a physical server rack buried deep within the permafrost. It is said she can identify a hardware failure simply by the change in the castle’s ambient temperature.
